To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reliability is a key issue for the successful commercialization of microsensors as well as micromechatronics, that the reliability issues are strongly application and system specific, that the reliability is not a property of the sensor or actuator itself, but of the entire system, that the reliability of microsystems is not only a function of the material properties but also of the design and manufacturing process, and that the reliability of the microsystems has to be addressed already at the early design stage.

(1) reliability is an integral part of the design process of microsensors, (2) the design for reliability has to be done at an early stage of development, (3) a systematic approach to reliability engineering in microsystem technology has to be established and (4) the reliability of a microsensor has to be evaluated in the context of its intended application.

the reliability of microsensors can be improved significantly by a proper design and by a proper manufacturing process, and that the reliability of micromechatronics actuators can be improved significantly if the actuator is designed as a system and not only as an actuator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability issues of the following microsystems: Inertial sensors (accelerometers, gyroscopes) Piezoelectric actuatores Hot film mass air flow (MAF) sensors
the reliability of automotive microsystems.

the following aspects: (1) the reliability of microsystems is determined by the reliability of the individual components and by the reliability of their interaction, (2) the reliability of the components is determined by the quality of their design, their manufacturing process, and by the environmental conditions they are exposed to, (3) the reliability of a system is determined by the interaction of all its components, (4) the interaction of components is determined by their design and the environmental conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reliability issues of microsystem components and their packaging can be solved in principle by means of a systematic engineering approach.
the reliability of microsensors is generally not a problem.
the reliability of microsensors as well as micromechatronics can be improved by a systematic approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

microsystem technology has already proven its reliability for automotive application, but that reliability aspects are still an essential part of the development of microsystem components and systems.
the reliability of microsensors can be improved significantly if one takes into account the special requirements of microsystems technology in the design and fabrication process.
reliability aspects of microsystems have to be considered in all development phases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of microsensors is not necessarily a problem of the sensor technology itself, but that the sensor is only one element of a complex system.

reliability issues in microsensors and actuators can only be addressed in a systematic and efficient way by a close cooperation of the microsensor/actuator manufacturer with the customer and the supplier of the respective electronic control unit.
the reliability of a microsensor or a micromechatronics actuator is not a given, but can be designed and optimized.
